title: Why Password Managers Still Matter
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article explaining why password managers still matter for ordinary consumers, what risks they reduce, what they do not solve, and practical criteria for choosing one without endorsing a specific vendor.
target_audience: non-technical consumers who understand basic online accounts but not security architecture

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: approve the pipeline's proposed thesis if it remains vendor-neutral and emphasizes risk reduction rather than perfect security
gate_script.postdraft: accept unless a required gate identifies a material factual or accessibility problem

title: Heat Pumps and Household Energy Costs
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article on when residential heat pumps lower household energy costs in the United States. Distinguish climate, electricity and fuel prices, building envelope, equipment efficiency, and incentives. Avoid a universal savings claim.
target_audience: homeowners comparing major HVAC options who can follow percentages and payback examples

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: approve a conditional thesis that savings depend on local operating conditions rather than asserting heat pumps are always cheaper
gate_script.approval: approved; present material regional conflicts neutrally
gate_script.postdraft: accept unless a required gate identifies unsupported savings claims

title: Does Remote Work Reduce Productivity?
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article evaluating whether remote work reduces productivity. Separate individual output, collaboration, innovation, retention, and management effects. Reconcile conflicting evidence rather than selecting one metric as definitive.
target_audience: business leaders and managers making workplace-policy decisions

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: approve a thesis that productivity effects are heterogeneous and measurement-dependent
gate_script.approval: approved; unresolved empirical conflicts must remain explicit
gate_script.postdraft: accept unless the article collapses productivity into a single unsupported metric

title: Passkeys Versus Passwords for Organizations
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article explaining the current practical tradeoffs between passkeys and passwords for organizations. Cover phishing resistance, recovery, device/platform support, deployment complexity, and coexistence with legacy authentication.
target_audience: IT and security leaders who understand MFA but are not identity-protocol specialists

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: approve a thesis that passkeys materially improve phishing resistance but migration and recovery design still determine deployment quality
gate_script.postdraft: accept unless current platform claims are stale or overstated

title: What Small Businesses Can Actually Automate With AI Agents
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article evaluating what small businesses can reliably automate with contemporary AI agents now, versus what still requires close supervision. Distinguish demonstrations from durable production use and include failure modes, economics, and operational controls.
target_audience: small-business owners and operations leaders evaluating near-term automation investments

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: approve a thesis that bounded workflows are more dependable than broad autonomous operation unless current evidence strongly supports a different conclusion
gate_script.approval: approved; present material capability disputes neutrally
gate_script.postdraft: address only material red-team findings; polish only high-priority reader gaps

title: What Soda Taxes Change—and What They Do Not
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article evaluating the evidence on sugar-sweetened beverage taxes. Separate purchase behavior, consumption, substitution, health outcomes, distributional effects, and use of tax revenue. Distinguish observational findings from causal evidence.
target_audience: policy-interested general readers comfortable with research summaries but not econometrics

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: approve a thesis proportional to the evidence; do not precommit to either advocacy or opposition
gate_script.approval: approved; retain unresolved causal and distributional conflicts explicitly
gate_script.postdraft: address material red-team findings that identify causal overstatement

title: Are Four-Day Workweeks Ready for Broad Adoption?
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article evaluating whether four-day workweeks are ready for broad adoption. Test a starting hypothesis that shorter workweeks generally preserve productivity while improving employee well-being. Actively revise or weaken that hypothesis if sector coverage, selection effects, or trial design do not support broad generalization.
target_audience: executives, HR leaders, and policy readers considering organizational adoption

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: confirm the stated starting hypothesis but explicitly authorize evidence-driven weakening
gate_script.approval: approved; if evidence challenges generalization, the final article must say so
gate_script.postdraft: address red-team findings about selection bias or external validity when material

title: Can Local Governments Measure AI Procurement Risk?
topic_prompt: Write a sourced article on how local governments can assess risk when procuring AI systems. Focus on measurable procurement controls, auditability, vendor documentation, evaluation limits, and where evidence is too thin to support confident claims about effectiveness.
target_audience: municipal technology, procurement, and policy officials

gate_script.thesis_confirmation: approve a thesis centered on verifiable procurement controls while requiring explicit uncertainty about outcome effectiveness
gate_script.approval: approved; insufficient evidence must remain visible rather than being filled with generic best practices
gate_script.postdraft: accept unless the article converts weak evidence into confident effectiveness claims
